JUDGMENT

Being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and award by which the Tribunal directed respondent No.1/owner to pay the compensation, this appeal is filed by petitioners under Section 173(1) of MV Act (1988) with a prayer to enhance the compensation.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.

3. It is the case of the petitioners that on 04.08.2008 at about 10:00 p.m. in the night hours, while deceased-Shabbir being the driver of tom-tom vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-31/A-161 proceeding towards Chigaralli cross, near Jagruthi Kendra road, Kellur village, the driver of Cruiser Jeep bearing Reg.No.KA-33/M-1461 came in a high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to said tom-tom vehicle.
Due to which the deceased-Shabbir sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries on the spot itself.
Thus, sought for allowing the petition.
As owner and insurer of the offending vehicle, respondents are liable to pay the compensation.
4. Upon service of notice, respondent No.1 remained absent and placed ex parte before the Tribunal.
5. Respondent No.2 appeared and filed written statement, denying the age, occupation, nature of injuries sustained and due to the injuries, deceased died.
It is further contended that the driver of the offending vehicle Cruiser Jeep bearing Reg.No.KA-33/M-1461 was not holding a valid licence on the date of accident.

The offending vehicle was not duly insured with respondent No.2, therefore,
respondent No.2 is not liable to pay any compensation to petitioners.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the petition.
6. Based on the pleadings, the Tribunal has framed necessary issues.
7. Petitioner No.2 has got examined himself as PW.1 and relied upon Exs.P1 to 7.

On behalf of respondents, respondent No.2 examined its official as RW.1 and got marked Exs.R1 to 3.
8.

Vide the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal partly allowed the claim petition granting compensation in a sum of Rs.2,77,000/- with interest @ 6% per annum and directed respondent No.1/owner to pay the same.

The details of the compensation granted are as under:
Sl.No. Heads Amount  1 Loss of dependency Rs.2,52,000/-
 2. Loss of estate Rs.10,000/-
 3. Loss of love and affection Rs.10,000/-
 4. Funeral expenses Rs.5,000/-
 Total Rs.2,77,000/-

2 9.
Heard arguments and perused the records.
10. During the course of argument, the learned counsel for the appellants contended that the Tribunal has not properly considering the income of the deceased.
The Tribunal has granted meager compensation on all the heads.
Hence, sought for allowing the appeal by enhancing the compensation.

11. Since the accident is of the year 2008, the income ought to have been taken at Rs.4,250/- p.m.
instead of Rs.3,000/- p.m. The deceased was aged 25 years, the appropriate multiplier would be 18.

However, the Tribunal has not added any compensation towards loss of future prospects as per Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram And Others1,
(Magma's case), 40% is required to be added towards loss of future prospects.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram And Others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the income is required to be taken at Rs.5,950/-.
Since the deceased was bachelor 50% is required to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.

With these components, the compensation under the head loss of dependency is Rs.5,950/- x 12 x 18 x 50% =
Rs.6,42,600/- as against Rs.2,52,000/- granted by the Tribunal.
12. As parents, petitioners are entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.40,000/- each i.e., (2018) 18 SCC 130 Rs.80,000/- under the head loss of consortium.
Similarly, Rs.15,000/- each awarded towards loss of estate and funeral expenses including transportation charges.

13. Thus, in all petitioners are entitled for total compensation in a sum of Rs.7,52,600/- as against Rs.2,77,000/- granted by the Tribunal as detailed below:
Sl. Heads Amount awarded Amount awarded No by the Tribunal by this Court 1. Loss of dependency Rs.2,52,000/- Rs.6,42,600/-
2. Loss of consortium Rs.10,000/- Rs.80,000/-
(love and affection)
3. Loss to estate Rs.10,000/- Rs.15,000/-
4. Funeral and Rs.5,000/- Rs.15,000/-
transportation charges Rs.2,77,000/- Rs.7,52,600/-
14.
Now coming to the question of liability.
However, the Tribunal has exonerated respondent No.2 from the liability on the ground that at the time of accident driver of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid driving licence.

However, as per the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pappu & Ors vs. Vinod Kumar Lamba & Anr.2, it was held that when the offending vehicle is insured, in the Jainabee W/O Late Baba Patel And Anr vs Mallangouda S/O Bassanagouda Hosamani ... on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13677267/
3 absence of the driver of offending vehicle possessing a valid driving licence, the insurance company is liable to pay the compensation and recover the same from the owner.

sentences.text: Therefore, in this case also it is necessary to direct respondent No.2/insurance company to pay the compensation with interest and recover the same from respondent No.1-owner.

15. To this extent, the appeal deserves to be modified and accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) Appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) Appellants/petitioners are entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.7,52,600/-
as against Rs.2,77,000/- granted by the Tribunal together with interest at 6% per annum.

(2018) 3 SCC 208 (iii) Respondent No.2/insurance company is directed to pay the compensation together with interest within a period of six weeks from the date of this order and recover the same from respondent No.1/owner.
(iv) Vide order dated 22.09.2014, the petitioners are not entitled to any interest on the enhanced compensation for the delayed period.
(v) The order of the Tribunal regarding apportionment, payment and deposit shall hold good for the enhanced compensation also.
(vi) The registry is directed to send a copy of this order to the Tribunal.
